title: Degree and Tate determinant have the same prime-adic absolute value
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of positive dimension, and let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$. For a group-scheme endomorphism $a:A\to A$ [def-sc-group-scheme], define $d(a)$ to be its isogeny degree, or zero if it is not an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny]. Let $V_\ell(a)$ be the induced endomorphism of the rational Tate module $V_\ell A$ [sk-def-av-tate]. Then, using the canonical image of $d(a)$ in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers],
$$|d(a)|_\ell=|\det(V_\ell(a)\mid V_\ell A)|_\ell.$$
Here determinant is [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. In particular this equality includes non-isogenies, when both sides are zero, and inseparable isogenies.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52, first display (isogeny case); positive-dimensional kernels and Tate rank give the non-isogeny case, as detailed in the report.

proof.text: Put $T=T_\ell A$, $V=V_\ell A$ and $h=2\dim A$. By [prop-av-tate-rank], choose a $\mathbf Z_\ell$-basis of $T$ of size $h$; the same basis gives $V=T\otimes\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $F$ be the matrix of $T_\ell(a)$, using the componentwise action of [sk-def-av-tate]. Its scalar extension represents $V_\ell(a)$, so their determinants, computed from these basis matrices as in [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant], are the same after $\mathbf Z_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 10.5, printed p.45; proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52

proof.text: For any abelian variety $C/k$ and $n\geq1$, projection to the $n$th coordinate induces $T_\ell C/\ell^nT_\ell C\simeq C[\ell^n](k)$. Indeed, repeatedly use [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective] with the positive integer $\ell$ to lift a point $x_n$ to $x_{n+1},x_{n+2},\ldots$ with $\ell x_{j+1}=x_j$, and set $x_j=\ell^{n-j}x_n$ below level $n$. These points have the required torsion orders. For a compatible sequence $t$ with $t_n=0$, the sequence $s_j=t_{j+n}$ is killed by $\ell^j$ and satisfies $\ell^ns=t$; conversely $\ell^nt$ has zero $n$th coordinate. This proves the kernel assertion and surjectivity directly from [sk-def-av-tate]. The identification commutes with $a$, by its coordinate formula. Thus $\ker(F\bmod\ell^n)$ is exactly $(\ker a)(k)[\ell^n]$.

source.place: Chapter I Remark 7.3, printed p.34; Proposition 10.5, printed p.45; finite-level expansion of p.52

proof.text: First suppose $a$ is an isogeny. By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], its kernel $K$ is a closed subgroup, and it is a finite commutative group scheme of order $d=d(a)$ by [def-sc-isogeny] and [lem-sc-av-commutative]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-group-scheme-primary-order] to $K$, with the given algebraically closed $k$ and invertible prime $\ell$. If $b=v_\ell(d)$, this gives $\#K(k)[\ell^n]=\ell^b$ for every $n\geq\max(1,b)$. In particular the kernels of $F\bmod\ell^n$ have this fixed cardinality for all such $n$. This uses the full scheme order $d$, so a nonreduced kernel is allowed.

source.place: Chapter I proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52, first and second equalities

proof.text:
Use [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] to view $\mathbf Z_\ell$ as a DVR with uniformizer $\ell$, and apply [lem-sfb-dvr-matrix-smith-powers] to $F$. Write its diagonal form as $r$ entries $\ell^{c_i}$ and $h-r$ zeros. The invertible basis matrices remain invertible modulo $\ell^n$. Multiplication by $\ell^c$ on $\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n\simeq\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ has kernel cardinality $\ell^{\min(c,n)}$: if $c<n$ the kernel consists of multiples of $\ell^{n-c}$, and if $c\geq n$ it is the whole ring. A zero diagonal entry contributes $\ell^n$. Hence
$$\#\ker(F\bmod\ell^n)=\ell^{n(h-r)+\sum_i\min(c_i,n)}.$$
Comparing with step 3 for arbitrarily large $n$ forces $r=h$; then taking $n$ at least all $c_i$ and $b$ gives $b=\sum_i c_i$. The two invertible basis matrices have unit determinants (their determinants multiply those of their inverses to $1$), so $|\det F|_\ell=\ell^{-\sum_i c_i}=\ell^{-b}=|d|_\ell$. This proves the isogeny case.

source.place: Chapter I proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52, final determinant/index equality, expanded by DVR Smith form

proof.text: Now suppose $a$ is not an isogeny. The kernel $H=\ker a$ is a closed subgroup scheme by [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]. By [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component], its reduced identity component $B$ is an abelian subvariety of $A$ and $\dim B=\dim H$. If $\dim B=0$, that node makes $H$ finite; since source and target of $a$ have equal dimension, [lem-sfb-finite-kernel-equal-dimension-isogeny] makes $a$ surjective, contradicting [def-sc-isogeny]. Hence $\dim B>0$. By [prop-av-tate-rank], $T_\ell B$ has positive rank. Its inclusion into $T_\ell A$ is injective: each coordinate is a point of the closed subgroup $B$, so equality of its images means equality of the coordinates. Choose a nonzero $t\in T_\ell B$. Its image is nonzero and is killed by $T_\ell(a)$, because $B\subset H$.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, printed p.32; reduced kernel discussion after Remark 10.2, printed p.43; Tate rank Proposition 10.5, printed p.45

proof.text: In the free coordinates of step 1, the nonzero image of $t$ remains nonzero over $\mathbf Q_\ell$: one of its coordinates is a nonzero element of the subring $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell$ of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Thus $V_\ell(a)$ has a nonzero kernel vector, so it is not invertible, and its determinant is zero by [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. By definition $d(a)=0$ in the non-isogeny case. Since $|0|_\ell=0$, the required equality holds here also.

source.place: Chapter I proof of Proposition 10.20, printed p.52; non-isogeny zero case expanded from the kernel and rank inputs

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement. Expanded Milne AV I p.52 into finite-level Tate projection, torsion cardinality and Smith determinant steps, then proved the non-isogeny case via the positive-dimensional reduced kernel. tool_uses.why: Generic abelian-variety Tate rank supplies integral and rational bases; no same-unit node gives rank.
Generic multiplication-surjectivity lifts finite torsion points to compatible Tate sequences.
Generic commutativity makes the isogeny kernel a commutative finite group scheme.
Generic DVR matrix normal form computes finite-level kernels and determinant norm.
Generic group-scheme kernel is a closed subgroup, needed for its reduced identity component.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q48-dfb0acd29 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's six steps and the new node lem-sfb-finite-group-scheme-primary-order in full, against Milne AV I printed p.52 (proof of Prop. 10.20, first display) and Milne iAG Prop. 11.3, Cor. 11.30 and Cor. 11.31. The item statement and source are unchanged from live, the live item is still unsplit, and there is no cycle (the closure has neither the item nor its only citer lem-sfb-abelian-tate-charpoly). No SGA is cited. Step 2's T/l^n identification (lifting by lem-sc-isogeny-surjective, kernel via the shifted sequence s_j=t_{j+n}) is correct, and kernel points come from lem-sc-kernel-subgroup. Step 3 applies the new node with the scheme order, so nonreduced kernels are covered. Step 4's Smith-form count l^{n(h-r)+sum min(c_i,n)} forces r=h and sum c_i=b; the unit determinants then give |det F|=|d|. Step 5: when a is not an isogeny, B=(H_red)^0 has positive dimension, because a 0-dimensional B makes H finite and lem-sfb-finite-kernel-equal-dimension-isogeny would then make a surjective, hence an isogeny. T_l B is nonzero, maps injectively into T_l A, and is killed by T_l(a). Step 6 then gives det=0. The new node is true via the connected-etale splitting: the connected order is a power of the characteristic exponent, then take the l-primary part of the finite abelian group. Tested on mu_p, alpha_p, Z/l^2 and mixed products. It does not duplicate lem-sc-connected-finite-order, lem-sc-fg-order-prime-etale, lem-sfb-finite-group-scheme-order-annihilator or lem-sfb-finite-commutative-group-local-constant-product (the last is an ingredient of its future proof). It is not a clause of the item. The stronger lem-sfb-isogeny-relative-tate-determinant (unsplit) was rightly not cited. Batch-5 flags: lem-sc-isogeny-surjective and prop-av-tate-rank reach def-trf-schematically-dense-open only through the general Nagata/Chow/Hilbert-polynomial chain. That chain is no part of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, so both citations are accepted. The declared tool_uses (generic abelian-variety, group-scheme and Smith-form tools) are accepted.
